course_name_original: Advanced methods for solving mathematical and algorithmic problems
course_name_en: Advanced methods for solving mathematical and algorithmic problems

learning_outcomes.text: The student knows: traditional problem solving methods, heuristic approaches towards that cannot be solved properly using traditional methods, AI/ML/DL techniques for NP-complete problems

The student is able to code proper solutions in a programming language of choice and to optimize the problem solving activity towards finding the optimal solution to any given problem or at least an acceptable candidate solution for NP-complete problems

The student has the ability to work independently to obtain a good understanding of the input data of any problem, to devise a proper algorithm for solving the problem using the adoption, adaption and improvement of taught techniques to the given problem and to properly evaluate the results obtained after applying the algorithm to solve the given problem

syllabus_topics: Data structures and their algorithms: linear, alinear noncyclic, cyclic
Should I Stay or Should I Go?
Traditional Algorithmic Methods: bruteforce/backtracking, divide and conquer, dynamic programming, greedy
Decision Trees. Information Gain out of Entropy. Expert Systems
NP Complete problems. Exploration vs Exploitation
Hill Climbing. Tabu Search. Simulated Annealing
Communities: Ant Colony Optimization, Particle Swarm Optimization
Graphs and networks: The Traveling Salesman Problem
Learning: data preprocessing and visualization, training, performance evaluation
Machine learning the basic logical and arithmetical operations
Hearing: Recurrent Neural Network, Long Short Term Memory
Quantum Logical Gates. The Quantum Computer
Implementing an ALU from logical gates
teaching_methods: Exposure: description, explanation, examples, discussion of case studies
assessment_rules: Each student should at least be able to employ traditional problem solving techniques and heuristic methods for solving mathematics and informatics problems. A final grade of at least 5 is required, cumulated from the points received for lab/seminary activities and the final oral examination from the exam session.
